confirm.text: Both of Campos's forms carry a multi-select string identical to the one on Michael Jobe's forms for the same two jobs, which suggests the selection was carried across the pair rather than made independently. That is the training point rather than a safety event.

These three are not the mis-selection pattern and should be treated as real: Michael Jobe's two forms (jobs 35167_1 and 35186_1) each carry a narrative naming a specific condition — a crew without a spotter, and personnel entering the work area — and in both cases the text says plainly that work was stopped. The record should show "Stop work authority utilized" on both. Separately, Ruben Rojo's job 35131_1 (XTO Energy, University 2-20 58H, 3:42 PM) selected "Unsafe conditions" while leaving the continued narrative, the entire Learn section, "What Went Well? Continued" and the Location Name all blank. With no positive narrative to offset the selection there is nothing to show conditions were in fact safe, so it needs Rojo's account of what he saw rather than being written off.

The inverse is also present. 1099 William Jimmy Cooper answered "No" to "Did we leave the location better than we found it?" on two forms — job 35188_2 ("It was muddy tried not to make worse") and job 35171_2 ("Muddy location") — without selecting "Unsafe conditions". Jacob Hernandez and Humberto Marquez-Salazar both recorded Oliver 704 as unreachable ("Road to well was muddy and no one could drive to it.") and neither selected it. Larry Jaramillo's facial-hair fit-test finding at Howard #9 likewise carries no selection. Conditions are being described in free text that the structured fields do not capture.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. In particular, fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images and not as text, so this review can confirm that a photo was taken and when, but not what it shows. Larry Jaramillo's missing extinguisher tag on trailer 507 surfaced only because he typed it into the comments field.

One further caveat specific to tonight: this review runs at 11:00 PM Central, an hour before the Central day closes, so any form submitted in the final hour of 10/01 is not in it. Submissions also routinely arrive hours late, sometimes the next morning — three of the forms read tonight carried 09/30 form dates. Any item above described as not received should be read as not received as of 11:00 PM, and a few may yet land overnight.

77 of 77 submissions read, plus the 3 prior-day submissions that arrived inside the window — 80 messages in total. The 10/01/2026 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin job boards from Blake Walton were available and were the boards used; 55 manned rows were checked for coverage.
